bull.b: Robust and improving cash generation (TTM operating cash flow ~$2.66B and FCF ~$2.50B) provides durable financial flexibility. High FCF conversion (~94% of net income) supports buybacks/dividends, funds strategic investments and cushions capital during cyclical credit or rate pressure.

Growing fee businesses—capital markets, wealth and private bank—reduce reliance on net interest income. Durable fee expansion improves revenue stability across rate cycles, raises fee-bearing client relationships, and increases cross-sell opportunities that sustainably enhance margins and ROE over the medium term.

Management’s Reimagine the Bank program with quantified savings and a clear efficiency target (mid-50s) is a structural lever to lift operating margins and ROTCE. If executed, the multi-year savings trajectory and branch optimization should sustainably improve returns and operating leverage.

bear.b: A CET1 ratio near 10.4% leaves limited excess capital versus internal targets. That modest cushion constrains organic capital deployment, may necessitate preferred issuance (as proposed), and reduces optionality for aggressive buybacks or faster balance-sheet growth without raising external capital.

Rising deposit betas and short-term FHLB reliance indicate structural funding pressure as loans grow faster than core deposits. Persistent deposit cost increases or continued wholesale funding would compress NIM over time and raise funding volatility risk, especially if competition for deposits intensifies.

bear.t: Loan mix shifts and elevated loss metrics
bear.b: Prolonged CRE runoff, a rising non-core auto balance and NCOs at ~37 bps signal mix and credit pressures. These trends can depress earning-asset yields, require higher provisions, and slow durable loan growth and margin recovery, sustaining headwinds to sustainable profitability near-term.
